chapter: War years, Decca records and La Conga
title: Hiring flexible jazz players instead of Latin musicians
summary: Machito says they picked adaptable American musicians who could be molded in phrasing rather than Latin players set in their ways.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: ......but he was a legitimate musician, you know a legitimate musician.

No, because I noticed that Mario, he wanted jazzmen or guys that played with jazzmen and I think that's where the Afro-Cuban sound, the Afro-Cuban jazz sound was born, when he kept replacing these guys with jazzmen.
Well, most of the people that was formerly jazz player, because there wasn't too many Latin musicians in New York......
In other words, the best musicians were the non-hispanic musicians, the ones that could read and the ones that were experienced.

There was a lot of good musicians that could read, but they have something, something that we were looking for. We were looking for people, flexible people, that we could mold the way we want the phrasing; and that's very hard when you had your mind, I mean, definite mind
about how to express yourself, to get in advance training or change your style. It's hard and when you get a piece of material and you polish the way you want.
All those Americans, on account they was American, they knew that they got to learn how to get adjusted with us.
That's what you were looking for then.

That's what we were looking for. A Spanish guy would have said: 'No, because I played with Coen, I played with Noro Morales, I played with Cugat .' We don't want that. We want a guy that would pay attention to what we want, because we know what we want. We are not from the old part of Cuba so we know how the Creole music should be played, and Mario know how to adopt the American arranger to the Cuban music so you had to be flexible in order to ta-ta-ta tara-ra, you know, the phrasing that was very important to us.
I see, so you selected special musicians.
Absolutely. They don't supposed to be the best musicians. The most flexible was the one that we was looking for.
